intro: Yes, an AI assistant for insurance claims adjusters can help on a Mac, mostly with email, notes and finding things on screen. Lazur is a voice assistant that sees your screen while you hold the shortcut, points at things and drafts text. It does not run Xactimate, and it does not click buttons for you.

Lazur runs on a Mac. It points, explains, drafts and dictates in Outlook, Excel, Word and Chrome.
Xactimate is not supported on a Mac, so keep estimating on a Windows machine for now.
Check your Outlook version first. Microsoft set an end date for legacy Outlook for Mac support.
Follow your carrier's rules on claim data before you paste anything into an AI tool.

blocks.text: Where a claims adjuster's day actually goes

No claims-specific survey gives a clean share of the day spent on email, typing or admin. That gap matters, so read any exact percentage with care. The best number on record measures compliance, not admin, and it comes from a 2019 study.

Rising's 2019 Workers' Compensation Benchmarking Study surveyed frontline claims professionals on compliance work. 58% spent more than 20% of their time on internal or external compliance activities. 14% spent more than 40% of their time on compliance.

Compliance is not the same as admin. It overlaps with paperwork, but it is wider. Lauren Cunningham of Sedgwick put it this way: “Compliance can become challenging when claim professionals are spending more time on paperwork and administrative tasks.” No percentage came with that remark.
What the job asks you to do every day

The Bureau of Labor Statistics describes the core work as careful review. Adjusters review documents and damaged property. Small details can have large financial consequences, so the review has to be careful.

Adjusters also compile photographs and recorded or written statements into reports for examiners. That means a lot of copying between a photo folder, a statement and a Word file. Most of that work happens on a screen.
Pay is steady. The BLS reports median pay of $78,020 per year, or $37.51 per hour, for the occupation in May 2025.

The outlook is shifting. BLS projects employment to decline 6 percent from 2025 to 2035. About 21,600 openings a year are expected, mostly from workers who transfer or leave the labor force. The handbook also says software will automate some tasks, such as evaluating photos of damaged property.

blocks.text: Why Xactimate and a Mac do not mix

Xactimate is the estimating tool many property adjusters use. Xactware's help page says the full set of tools needs Windows. It reads: “To utilize all the tools in Xactimate online, a Windows operating system is required.” It adds: “Mac is not supported at this time.”

The page also says Xactimate online needs the Xactware ClickOnce browser extension to open and edit projects. Third-party cookies and pop-ups must not be blocked. For XactAdmin on a Mac, Xactware recommends Chrome.
Some blogs say the web version works in any browser. Xactware's own page says otherwise. When a vendor page and a blog disagree, trust the vendor page. Then ask your IT team to confirm.
What to do if you have a Mac but estimating needs Windows

items: Ask your IT team whether a Windows machine or Windows desktop is available for estimating.
Keep Xactimate work on that machine. Keep email, notes and reports on your Mac.
Lazur is a Mac app. It does not run on a Windows machine, so it cannot help inside Xactimate there.
Ask whether your carrier allows AI help on a Mac that holds claim files before you start.

blocks.text: Do not treat the Mac as a dead end. Much of the day runs on email, documents and spreadsheets. Those tools all run on a Mac, and that is where voice help earns its keep.
Outlook for Mac: check your version before you set anything up

Outlook carries most of the claim traffic. Start by checking which Outlook you run. Microsoft's Outlook for Mac page describes the new Outlook. It lists a customizable toolbar, search powered by Microsoft Search, a My Day task pane, replies without opening a new compose window, Snooze and suggested meeting times.

Open the Help menu. If you see Revert to Legacy Outlook, you run the new Outlook. Microsoft says accounts added in the new Outlook do not carry over to Legacy Outlook, and the reverse also applies. Add each account once, in the version you plan to keep.

blocks.title: Check the end date
blocks.text: Microsoft's Outlook for Mac page says support for legacy Outlook for Mac will end in October 2026. That date has passed as of today, so check Microsoft's current status before you plan a switch. Support also depends on your Microsoft 365, Office or Outlook license.

For claim-specific setup, read [Outlook for insurance claims adjusters on Mac](/for/insurance-claims-adjusters/outlook). For calendar steps, see [how to create a calendar event in Outlook on Mac](/how-to/create-a-calendar-event-in-outlook).
Excel and Word: keep the tracker and the report in sync

Two files carry most of a claim. The Excel tracker holds dates, amounts and next steps. The Word report holds the inspection narrative and the photo list. Most errors happen when those two files drift apart.

Here is a worked example. A shop sends a supplement on a Tuesday. Your tracker needs the new amount and a follow-up date. Your report needs a new paragraph. Your Outlook reply needs the same amount, too.

items: Update the amount and follow-up date in the Excel tracker first.
Add a dated paragraph to the Word report.
Reply in Outlook with the same amount, then ask Lazur to read the draft aloud before you send.

blocks.text: Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask Lazur about anything on screen. Ask what a formula does, or ask for one that flags files with no activity for a set time. Lazur answers out loud and points at the cell it means. See [Excel for insurance claims adjusters on Mac](/for/insurance-claims-adjusters/excel) for tracker layouts.

In Word, ask Lazur to walk you through a comment or a header. For the exact steps, use [how to add a comment in Word on Mac](/how-to/add-a-comment-in-word) or [how to add a header in Word on Mac](/how-to/add-a-header-in-word).
Dictating inspection notes without losing the details
Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Dictation helps most with the notes you would otherwise type after a site visit, when your hands are full of photos and keys.

Dictation misses names, part numbers and policy terms. Teach it the words you use most with the personal dictionary. Use snippets for sentences you repeat, such as a standard closing line for each report.

Try this with a site note. Say: “Vehicle parked on the street. Rear bumper cracked, left panel dented. No airbag deployment seen. Photos taken from all sides.” Read the text back before you save. Dictation gets the words right. It does not check the facts.
Clipboard slots help when you need a claim number in two places. Copy the number from Outlook into a slot, then paste it into Word and the tracker. That saves a trip back to the email.
When a claim crosses two machines
Some claims start on your Mac and finish on a Windows estimating machine. The risk sits in the handoff. An amount typed twice is an amount that can differ.
Keep one source of truth. Use the Excel tracker as the master list. Copy numbers from it, not from memory or an old email. Then ask Lazur to draft the update so the amounts match the tracker.

Research helps here too. Ask Lazur to research a topic, such as typical repair times for a vehicle type. It works in its own Chrome tabs and returns a summary and a report. Check each source before you use a figure.
Claim data, employer rules and what not to paste

Claim files hold personal and financial details about policyholders and third parties. Your employer and your carrier set the rules for that data. Follow those rules before you use any AI tool on a live file.

Here is how Lazur handles what you say and show. It listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer, and they are not stored. Content is not used to train AI models.
Those are product facts, not a promise about your carrier's rules. This page does not claim any compliance certification for claims data. Your compliance team decides what goes into an AI tool.
Ask your compliance team these questions first:

items: Can I use an AI assistant on live claim files, or only on templates?
Can dictated notes that name a claimant go into the claim system?
Do Mac tools need separate approval before we use them on claims?

blocks.text: Mistakes adjusters make with AI tools

items: Sending a draft without checking the amounts, dates and claim numbers in it.
Trusting an answer about policy wording without reading the clause on the page.
Dictating names and part numbers, then missing a wrong spelling.
Pasting a whole claim file into a personal chat window.
Assuming a web estimating tool runs on a Mac because a blog said so.

blocks.text: Most of these mistakes come from speed. Slow down at the points where money or a deadline changes hands. A quick check there costs less than a corrected payment.
A simple first week with voice help
Pick one task, not the whole job. Replies to shops and dictated site notes are good starting points. Run that one task for a week, then decide whether to add another.

items: Set up Outlook first, then confirm which version you run.
Dictate every site note for a few days, and check each one before it is saved.
Ask Lazur to explain one policy clause a day, then read that clause yourself.
Write down each thing Lazur got wrong, and each time it saved you a trip.

blocks.text: When you are ready, [download Lazur for Mac](/download). Check [current plans on the pricing page](/pricing) for trial terms, since plans can change.
What the research does not settle

Several gaps remain. No claims-specific source gives a reliable share of the day spent on email or typing. The 2019 Rising numbers measure compliance, not admin, and the article does not state a sample size.
Guidewire ClaimCenter browser and operating system support could not be verified for this page. Your insurer's version and hosting decide what works on a Mac. Ask your claims system admin.

Microsoft's end date for legacy Outlook for Mac has already passed. Check Microsoft's current status before you plan a move. The Xactimate Mac statement also carries no date, so confirm it with Xactware.
The fix for each gap is local. Your IT team and your claims system admin can answer these questions in one meeting.

faq.question: Can an AI assistant see my claim file?
faq.answer: Lazur looks at your screen only while you hold ⌥ ⌘. It answers about what is on that screen. It does not open your claim system on its own, and it does not click buttons for you.

faq.question: Does Lazur run Xactimate on a Mac?
faq.answer: No. Xactware says Mac is not supported for Xactimate online at this time, and Lazur does not operate other apps for you. Use Lazur for email, notes and reports. Do estimating on Windows if your carrier provides it.

faq.question: Which Outlook should a claims adjuster use on a Mac?
faq.answer: Check the Help menu for Revert to Legacy Outlook. Microsoft says legacy support was set to end in October 2026, and that date has passed. Confirm the current status on Microsoft's page and ask your IT team which version they support.

faq.question: Can I dictate claim notes straight into the claim system?
faq.answer: Hold fn to dictate at the cursor in any app. Whether a claim system field accepts dictated text depends on that field. Read the result before you save it, and follow your carrier's rules on what goes into notes.

faq.question: Is Lazur approved for claims data?
faq.answer: This page does not claim any compliance certification for Lazur or for claims data. Your employer's rules decide what you can share with an AI tool. Ask your compliance team before you use it on live files.

faq.question: How much time will voice help save?
faq.answer: No claims-specific source gives a reliable saving figure. Track your own time on one task for a week, with and without voice help, then compare the two results.

faq.question: Does Lazur work on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur runs on macOS, on both Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available.

faq.question: Will Lazur work inside Guidewire ClaimCenter?
faq.answer: Lazur can look at whatever is on a Mac screen while you hold the shortcut. ClaimCenter browser and operating system support could not be verified here, so ask your claims system admin how your insurer runs it.
